subject.title: fix(find): prevent recursive re-entry in child kill via sentinel guard (#98961)

question: Should this PR require real OpenClaw find/fd child-error proof before merge, or should a maintainer explicitly accept the source-level lifecycle change without that proof?
rationale: The code path is source-reproducible and the sentinel matches Node kill-error behavior, but the contributor has not shown an inspectable after-fix run through the patched OpenClaw find tool.

options.title: Require real find-path proof
options.body: Ask for redacted terminal output, logs, or a linked artifact that runs the patched OpenClaw find tool through an fd spawn/error, abort, or kill-failure cleanup path.

options.title: Accept source-level override
options.body: A maintainer can intentionally accept the guarded lifecycle change from source and Node contract review despite the missing real-behavior proof.

options.title: Request narrower cleanup shape
options.body: Ask the contributor to call the guarded stop hook only from the child error path if shared cleanup is considered too broad.

recommendation.title: Require real find-path proof
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted terminal output, logs, or a linked artifact that runs the patched OpenClaw find tool through an fd spawn/error, abort, or kill-failure cleanup path.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor directly requested source-level review from this handle, and path history shows strong recent ownership of find/grep session-tool behavior.
